# Traefik — Installation Plan & Execution Record

## Project Overview

**Traefik** is a cloud-native HTTP reverse proxy and Kubernetes Ingress controller. It dynamically discovers routing rules from Kubernetes resources and forwards traffic to backend services. Evaluated for OpenTelemetry maturity.

- **Chart**: `traefik/traefik`
- **Chart version**: `40.2.0`
- **App version**: `v3.7.1`
- **Namespace**: `traefik`
- **Helm repo**: `https://traefik.github.io/charts`

---

## Installation Method

```bash
helm repo add traefik https://traefik.github.io/charts
helm repo update traefik
kubectl create namespace traefik --context kind-otel-eval-traefik
helm upgrade --install traefik traefik/traefik \
    --version 40.2.0 \
    --namespace traefik \
    --kube-context kind-otel-eval-traefik \
    -f .otel-eval/traefik/traefik/values.yaml \
    --wait --timeout 5m
```

> **Note**: The `--wait` flag times out (5m) in kind clusters because the `LoadBalancer` service type never gets an external IP assigned. The pod runs successfully — the timeout is a Helm readiness check artifact, not a real failure. The service type is set to `ClusterIP` in values.yaml to avoid this.

---

## Telemetry Configuration

### Traces — OTLP gRPC

Traefik v3 has native OTel SDK integration. Configured via Helm values:

```yaml
tracing:
  addInternals: true          # trace internal dashboard/ping routes too
  serviceName: traefik
  sampleRate: 1.0             # 100% sampling for evaluation
  otlp:
    enabled: true
    grpc:
      enabled: true
      endpoint: "otel-collector-opentelemetry-collector.opentelemetry.svc.cluster.local:4317"
      insecure: true
```

### Metrics — OTLP gRPC push + Prometheus scrape

Two metrics channels are active simultaneously:

**OTLP push** (Traefik → Collector):
```yaml
metrics:
  addInternals: true
  otlp:
    enabled: true
    addEntryPointsLabels: true
    addRoutersLabels: true
    addServicesLabels: true
    pushInterval: "10s"
    grpc:
      enabled: true
      endpoint: "otel-collector-opentelemetry-collector.opentelemetry.svc.cluster.local:4317"
      insecure: true
```

**Prometheus scrape** (Collector → Traefik):
```yaml
metrics:
  prometheus:
    entryPoint: metrics
    addEntryPointsLabels: true
    addRoutersLabels: true
    addServicesLabels: true
    service:
      enabled: true   # creates traefik-metrics ClusterIP service on port 9100
```

### Logs — OTLP gRPC (experimental feature gate)

OTLP log export requires enabling `experimental.otlpLogs`:

```yaml
experimental:
  otlpLogs: true

logs:
  general:
    format: json
    level: INFO
  access:
    enabled: true
    format: json
    otlp:
      enabled: true
      grpc:
        enabled: true
        endpoint: "otel-collector-opentelemetry-collector.opentelemetry.svc.cluster.local:4317"
        insecure: true
```

---

## Collector Changes

The OTel Collector `values.yaml` was updated to add a Prometheus scrape target for Traefik:

```yaml
receivers:
  prometheus:
    config:
      scrape_configs:
        - job_name: traefik
          scrape_interval: 15s
          static_configs:
            - targets:
                - traefik-metrics.traefik.svc.cluster.local:9100
```

The `prometheus` receiver was also added to the metrics pipeline:

```yaml
service:
  pipelines:
    metrics:
      receivers: [otlp, k8s_cluster, prometheus]
```

The collector was upgraded:
```bash
helm upgrade otel-collector open-telemetry/opentelemetry-collector \
    --namespace opentelemetry \
    -f .otel-eval/traefik/collector/values.yaml \
    --wait
```

---

## Routing Setup

A Kubernetes Ingress resource was created to route traffic through Traefik to the test backend:

**File**: `.otel-eval/traefik/traefik/routing/ingress.yaml`

```yaml
apiVersion: networking.k8s.io/v1
kind: Ingress
metadata:
  name: otel-eval-backend
  namespace: demo
spec:
  ingressClassName: traefik
  rules:
  - http:
      paths:
      - path: /
        pathType: Prefix
        backend:
          service:
            name: otel-eval-backend
            port:
              number: 3000
```

Applied with:
```bash
kubectl apply -f .otel-eval/traefik/traefik/routing/ingress.yaml --context kind-otel-eval-traefik
```

---

## Traffic Generation

Access via port-forward (kind cluster has no LoadBalancer IP):

```bash
nohup kubectl port-forward -n traefik svc/traefik 18080:80 --context kind-otel-eval-traefik > /tmp/pf-traefik.log 2>&1 < /dev/null &
```

Traffic pattern:
- 10 normal `GET /` requests
- 5 requests with `traceparent` header (trace context propagation test)
- 5 `GET /health` requests
- 3 `GET /nonexistent` requests (404 path)

```bash
# Normal requests
for i in $(seq 1 10); do curl -s http://localhost:18080/ > /dev/null; sleep 0.3; done

# With trace context
for i in $(seq 1 5); do
  curl -s -H "traceparent: 00-4bf92f3577b34da6a3ce929d0e0e4736-00f067aa0ba902b7-01" \
    http://localhost:18080/ > /dev/null
  sleep 0.3
done

# Health checks
for i in $(seq 1 5); do curl -s http://localhost:18080/health > /dev/null; sleep 0.2; done

# 404s
for i in $(seq 1 3); do curl -s http://localhost:18080/nonexistent > /dev/null; sleep 0.2; done
```

### Traces

- **Status**: Flowing via OTLP gRPC
- **Span names observed**: `GET`, `ReverseProxy`, `middleware - query`, `middleware - jsonParser`, `middleware - expressInit`, `middleware - <anonymous>`, `request handler - /`, `GET /`
- **Instrumentation scope**: `github.com/traefik/traefik`
- **W3C Trace Context propagation**: Confirmed — incoming `traceparent` trace ID (`4bf92f3577b34da6a3ce929d0e0e4736`) preserved, new child span IDs generated for each hop

### Metrics

- **Status**: Flowing via both OTLP gRPC push and Prometheus scrape
- **Traefik-native OTLP metrics observed**: `traefik_config_reloads_total`, `traefik_config_last_reload_success`, `traefik_open_connections`, `traefik_entrypoint_requests_total`, `traefik_entrypoint_request_duration_seconds`, `traefik_entrypoint_requests_bytes_total`, `traefik_entrypoint_responses_bytes_total`, `traefik_router_requests_total`, `traefik_router_request_duration_seconds`, `traefik_router_requests_bytes_total`, `traefik_router_responses_bytes_total`
- **OTel semantic convention metrics**: `http.server.request.duration`, `http.client.request.duration`

### Logs

- **Status**: Flowing via OTLP gRPC (experimental feature)
- **Type**: Access logs with rich per-request attributes
- **Trace correlation**: `trace_id` and `span_id` present in log attributes
- **Notable quirk**: Log body is a JSON string (the full access log line embedded as a string), not a structured object. This is a known Traefik serialization behavior.
